title: The genealogy of Jesus
summary: Jesus' family line from Abraham through David and the exile to Joseph, in three sets of fourteen generations, naming Tamar, Rahab, Ruth and 'the wife of Uriah'.

title: The birth of Jesus and Joseph's dream
summary: Mary is found to be with child from the Holy Spirit. An angel tells Joseph in a dream to take her as his wife and to name the child Jesus (Immanuel, 'God with us').

title: The visit of the wise men (Magi)
summary: Wise men from the east follow a star to Bethlehem, bring gold, frankincense and myrrh, and are warned in a dream not to return to Herod.

title: The flight to Egypt
summary: An angel warns Joseph, and he takes Mary and the child to Egypt ('Out of Egypt I called my son').

title: Herod kills the children of Bethlehem
summary: Herod orders all boys two years old and under in Bethlehem killed, fulfilling Jeremiah's 'Rachel weeping for her children'.

title: The return to Nazareth
summary: After Herod dies, Joseph returns but avoids Archelaus's Judea and settles in Nazareth: 'He shall be called a Nazarene.'

title: John the Baptist prepares the way
summary: John preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judea, wearing camel's hair and eating locusts and wild honey, and calls the Pharisees and Sadducees a 'brood of vipers'.

title: The baptism of Jesus
summary: John baptizes Jesus in the Jordan. The Spirit descends like a dove and a voice says, 'This is my beloved Son.'

title: The temptation of Jesus
summary: After fasting forty days, Jesus is tempted by the devil three times (stones to bread, the temple pinnacle, all the kingdoms) and answers each with Scripture.

title: Jesus begins his ministry in Galilee
summary: After John is arrested, Jesus moves to Capernaum, fulfilling Isaiah's 'people dwelling in darkness have seen a great light', and preaches 'Repent, for the kingdom of heaven is at hand.'

title: Jesus calls the first disciples
summary: By the Sea of Galilee Jesus calls Peter and Andrew, then James and John, to be 'fishers of men'.

title: Jesus teaches and heals great crowds
summary: Jesus goes throughout Galilee teaching, proclaiming the gospel and healing every disease; crowds follow from the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea and beyond the Jordan.

title: The Beatitudes (Sermon on the Mount begins)
summary: On a mountain Jesus blesses the poor in spirit, mourners, the meek, the hungry for righteousness, the merciful, the pure in heart, peacemakers and the persecuted.

title: Salt and light
summary: 'You are the salt of the earth... You are the light of the world.' Let your good works shine so others glorify your Father.

title: Christ came to fulfill the Law
summary: Jesus came not to abolish but to fulfill the Law and the Prophets; your righteousness must exceed that of the scribes and Pharisees.

title: Anger (murder)
summary: Being angry with or insulting a brother brings judgment; be reconciled before offering your gift at the altar, and settle with your accuser quickly.

title: Lust (adultery)
summary: Looking at a woman with lustful intent is adultery in the heart; if your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out.

title: Divorce (Sermon on the Mount)
summary: Whoever divorces his wife, except for sexual immorality, makes her commit adultery.

title: Oaths
summary: Do not swear at all, by heaven, earth, Jerusalem or your head; let your 'Yes' be 'Yes' and your 'No' be 'No'.

title: Retaliation (an eye for an eye)
summary: Do not resist the one who is evil: turn the other cheek, give your cloak too, go the second mile, give to the one who begs.

title: Love your enemies
summary: Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, for the Father sends sun and rain on the just and unjust; be perfect as your Father is perfect.

title: Giving to the needy
summary: Do not practice righteousness to be seen; when you give, do not sound a trumpet and do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.

title: Praying in secret
summary: Do not pray like the hypocrites on street corners or heap up empty phrases like the Gentiles; pray to your Father in secret.

title: The Lord's Prayer
summary: 'Our Father in heaven, hallowed be your name...' followed by the warning that if you do not forgive others, your Father will not forgive you.

title: Fasting
summary: When you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites; anoint your head and wash your face so your fasting is seen only by your Father.

title: Treasures in heaven
summary: Do not lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust destroy; where your treasure is, there your heart will be also.

title: The eye is the lamp of the body
summary: If your eye is healthy your whole body will be full of light; if it is bad, how great is the darkness.

title: No one can serve two masters
summary: You cannot serve God and money.

title: Do not be anxious
summary: Look at the birds of the air and the lilies of the field; seek first the kingdom of God and his righteousness, and do not be anxious about tomorrow.

title: Judging others (the speck and the log)
summary: Judge not, that you be not judged; take the log out of your own eye first; do not throw pearls before pigs.

title: Ask, seek, knock
summary: Ask and it will be given; if evil fathers give good gifts instead of a stone or a serpent, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things.

title: The Golden Rule
summary: Whatever you wish that others would do to you, do also to them, for this is the Law and the Prophets.

title: The narrow gate
summary: The gate is wide and the way easy that leads to destruction; narrow is the gate and hard the way that leads to life, and those who find it are few.

title: A tree and its fruit (false prophets)
summary: Beware of false prophets in sheep's clothing; you will recognize them by their fruits.

title: 'I never knew you'
summary: Not everyone who says 'Lord, Lord' will enter the kingdom, but the one who does the Father's will.

title: The wise and foolish builders
summary: The one who hears and does Jesus' words builds on the rock; the one who does not builds on sand, and his house falls.

title: The crowds are astonished at his authority
summary: The Sermon on the Mount ends; the crowds are astonished because he teaches as one with authority, not as their scribes.

title: Jesus cleanses a leper
summary: A leper says 'Lord, if you will, you can make me clean.' Jesus touches him, heals him and sends him to show himself to the priest.

title: The faith of the centurion
summary: A centurion in Capernaum asks Jesus only to say the word to heal his servant; Jesus marvels that he has not found such faith in Israel.

title: Peter's mother-in-law and many others healed
summary: Jesus heals Peter's mother-in-law of a fever and that evening heals many, fulfilling 'He took our illnesses and bore our diseases.'

title: The cost of following Jesus
summary: To an eager scribe: 'Foxes have holes... but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.' To a disciple: 'Leave the dead to bury their own dead.'

title: Jesus calms the storm
summary: Jesus sleeps in the boat during a great storm, rebukes the disciples' little faith, then rebukes the winds and sea.

title: The two demon-possessed men of the Gadarenes
summary: Jesus casts demons out of two fierce men into a herd of pigs, which rush into the sea; the town begs him to leave.

title: Jesus heals a paralytic
summary: Jesus tells a paralytic his sins are forgiven; when scribes call it blasphemy, he heals him to show the Son of Man has authority to forgive sins.

title: Jesus calls Matthew
summary: Jesus calls Matthew from the tax booth and eats with tax collectors and sinners: 'I came not to call the righteous, but sinners.'

title: A question about fasting (new wine, old wineskins)
summary: John's disciples ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast; the wedding guests do not mourn while the bridegroom is with them. No one puts new wine into old wineskins.

title: A ruler's daughter raised and a woman healed
summary: On the way to raise a ruler's dead daughter, Jesus heals a woman with a twelve-year discharge of blood who touched the fringe of his garment.

title: Jesus heals two blind men
summary: Two blind men cry 'Have mercy on us, Son of David'; Jesus touches their eyes: 'According to your faith be it done to you.'

title: Jesus heals a man who could not speak
summary: Jesus casts a demon out of a mute man; the crowds marvel, but the Pharisees say he casts out demons by the prince of demons.

title: The harvest is plentiful, the laborers few
summary: Seeing the crowds harassed and helpless like sheep without a shepherd, Jesus has compassion and tells the disciples to pray for laborers.

title: The twelve apostles
summary: Jesus gives the twelve authority over unclean spirits and disease; the apostles are named, from Simon Peter to Judas Iscariot.

title: Jesus sends out the twelve
summary: Go only to the lost sheep of Israel; heal, raise the dead, take no money or bag; shake the dust off your feet where you are not received.

title: Persecution will come
summary: 'I am sending you out as sheep in the midst of wolves, so be wise as serpents and innocent as doves'; the one who endures to the end will be saved.

title: Have no fear of them
summary: Do not fear those who kill the body; not one sparrow falls apart from your Father, and the hairs of your head are numbered. Whoever acknowledges me before men, I will acknowledge.

title: Not peace, but a sword
summary: Jesus will set family members against one another; whoever loves father or mother more is not worthy; whoever loses his life for my sake will find it.

title: Rewards (a cup of cold water)
summary: Whoever receives you receives me; whoever gives a little one a cup of cold water will by no means lose his reward.

title: Messengers from John the Baptist
summary: From prison John asks, 'Are you the one who is to come?' Jesus answers: the blind see, the lame walk, the dead are raised, the poor hear good news.

title: Jesus' testimony about John (children in the marketplace)
summary: John is more than a prophet, the Elijah who is to come; this generation is like children who complain, rejecting both John and the Son of Man.

title: Woe to unrepentant cities
summary: Jesus denounces Chorazin, Bethsaida and Capernaum: Tyre, Sidon and Sodom would have repented had they seen his mighty works.

title: Come to me and I will give you rest
summary: The Father has hidden these things from the wise and revealed them to little children; 'Come to me, all who labor... my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.'

title: Lord of the Sabbath (grain fields)
summary: When the disciples pick grain on the Sabbath, Jesus cites David and the priests: 'Something greater than the temple is here... the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.'

title: A man with a withered hand
summary: In the synagogue Jesus heals a withered hand on the Sabbath ('it is lawful to do good'); the Pharisees plot to destroy him.

title: God's chosen servant
summary: Jesus withdraws, heals many and orders them not to make him known, fulfilling Isaiah: 'a bruised reed he will not break.'

title: Blasphemy against the Spirit (Jesus and Beelzebul)
summary: Accused of casting out demons by Beelzebul, Jesus says a house divided cannot stand; blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

title: A tree is known by its fruit (careless words)
summary: 'Out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks'; people will give account for every careless word.

title: The sign of Jonah
summary: An evil generation seeks a sign; none will be given but Jonah's: three days and nights in the heart of the earth. Something greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.

title: The return of an unclean spirit
summary: An unclean spirit leaves a man, finds the house empty and swept, and returns with seven worse spirits; so it will be with this evil generation.

title: Jesus' mother and brothers
summary: Told his family is outside, Jesus points to his disciples: whoever does the will of my Father is my brother and sister and mother.

title: The parable of the sower
summary: Teaching from a boat, Jesus tells of seed falling on the path, rocky ground, among thorns and on good soil yielding a hundredfold.

title: The purpose of the parables
summary: To the disciples it is given to know the secrets of the kingdom; to others he speaks in parables, fulfilling Isaiah's 'seeing they do not see.'

title: The parable of the sower explained
summary: The seed is the word: snatched by the evil one, withered by persecution, choked by cares and riches, or bearing fruit in one who understands.

title: The parable of the weeds (wheat and tares)
summary: An enemy sows weeds among wheat; the master lets both grow until the harvest, then gathers the weeds to burn and the wheat into the barn.

title: The parable of the mustard seed
summary: The kingdom is like the smallest of seeds that becomes a tree where birds nest.

title: The parable of the leaven
summary: The kingdom is like leaven a woman hid in three measures of flour until all was leavened.

title: Prophecy and parables
summary: Jesus says nothing to the crowds without a parable, fulfilling 'I will open my mouth in parables.'

title: The parable of the weeds explained
summary: The sower is the Son of Man, the field the world, the weeds the sons of the evil one, the harvest the end of the age; the righteous will shine like the sun.

title: The parable of the hidden treasure
summary: A man finds treasure in a field and in his joy sells all he has to buy that field.

title: The parable of the pearl of great value
summary: A merchant finds one pearl of great value and sells all he has to buy it.

title: The parable of the net
summary: A net gathers fish of every kind; the good are kept and the bad thrown away, so the angels will separate the evil from the righteous.

title: New and old treasures (the master of a house)
summary: Every scribe trained for the kingdom is like a master of a house who brings out of his treasure what is new and what is old.

title: Jesus rejected at Nazareth
summary: His hometown takes offense ('Is not this the carpenter's son?'); 'A prophet is not without honor except in his hometown.' He does few mighty works there because of their unbelief.

title: The death of John the Baptist
summary: Herod the tetrarch, who had imprisoned John over Herodias, has him beheaded at the request of Herodias's daughter after she dances at his birthday.

title: Jesus feeds the five thousand
summary: With five loaves and two fish Jesus feeds about five thousand men besides women and children; twelve baskets are left over.

title: Jesus walks on the water
summary: Jesus walks on the sea in the fourth watch; Peter walks toward him, sinks when he sees the wind, and is saved. The disciples worship him as the Son of God.

title: Jesus heals the sick in Gennesaret
summary: The sick beg to touch the fringe of his garment, and as many as touch it are made well.

title: Traditions and commandments (unwashed hands)
summary: Pharisees complain that the disciples do not wash their hands; Jesus says they void God's command to honor parents for their tradition ('This people honors me with their lips').

title: What defiles a person
summary: Not what goes into the mouth but what comes out of the heart defiles; the Pharisees are blind guides.

title: The faith of a Canaanite woman
summary: In the region of Tyre and Sidon a Canaanite woman persists for her demon-oppressed daughter ('even the dogs eat the crumbs'); Jesus praises her great faith.

title: Jesus heals many by the Sea of Galilee
summary: On a mountain Jesus heals the lame, blind, crippled and mute, and the crowd glorifies the God of Israel.

title: Jesus feeds the four thousand
summary: With seven loaves and a few small fish Jesus feeds four thousand men besides women and children; seven baskets are left over.

title: The Pharisees and Sadducees demand a sign
summary: You can read the sky but not the signs of the times; no sign will be given except the sign of Jonah.

title: The leaven of the Pharisees and Sadducees
summary: The disciples think Jesus is talking about bread; he means the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.

title: Peter confesses Jesus as the Christ
summary: At Caesarea Philippi Peter says, 'You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.' Jesus: 'On this rock I will build my church' and gives him the keys of the kingdom.

title: Jesus foretells his death; 'Get behind me, Satan'
summary: Jesus begins to show he must suffer, be killed and be raised; Peter rebukes him and Jesus calls him a hindrance.

title: Take up your cross
summary: Deny yourself and take up your cross; what will it profit a man if he gains the whole world and forfeits his soul?

title: The Transfiguration
summary: On a high mountain Jesus' face shines like the sun before Peter, James and John; Moses and Elijah appear, and a voice says 'listen to him'. Coming down, Jesus says Elijah has already come (John the Baptist).

title: Jesus heals a boy with a demon (faith like a mustard seed)
summary: The disciples cannot heal an epileptic boy; Jesus rebukes the demon and says faith like a mustard seed can move mountains.

title: Jesus foretells his death a second time
summary: Gathered in Galilee, Jesus says he will be delivered, killed and raised on the third day; the disciples are greatly distressed.

title: The temple tax (the coin in the fish)
summary: Asked whether Jesus pays the two-drachma tax, Jesus sends Peter to catch a fish with a shekel in its mouth to pay for them both.

title: Who is the greatest? (become like children)
summary: Jesus sets a child among them: whoever humbles himself like this child is greatest; better a millstone than to cause a little one to sin.

title: Temptations to sin
summary: Woe to the world for temptations; if your hand, foot or eye causes you to sin, cut it off or tear it out.

title: The parable of the lost sheep
summary: Do not despise little ones; a shepherd leaves the ninety-nine to seek the one that went astray. It is not the Father's will that one of these little ones perish.

title: If your brother sins against you (church discipline)
summary: Go to him alone, then with one or two witnesses, then tell the church; what you bind on earth is bound in heaven; where two or three are gathered, I am among them.

title: How often to forgive (seventy-seven times)
summary: Peter asks if he should forgive seven times; Jesus says seventy-seven times.

title: The parable of the unforgiving servant
summary: A servant forgiven ten thousand talents throttles a fellow servant who owes him a hundred denarii; the king hands him to the jailers.

title: Teaching about divorce
summary: Pharisees test Jesus on divorce; from the beginning the two become one flesh: 'What God has joined together, let not man separate.' Some are eunuchs for the kingdom.

title: Let the little children come to me
summary: The disciples rebuke those bringing children; Jesus says to such belongs the kingdom of heaven and lays his hands on them.

title: The rich young man
summary: A young man asks what good deed brings eternal life; told to sell his possessions and follow Jesus, he goes away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.

title: A camel through the eye of a needle (the reward of the twelve)
summary: It is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom; with God all things are possible. The twelve will sit on twelve thrones; the first will be last.

title: The parable of the laborers in the vineyard
summary: A master hires workers throughout the day and pays all a denarius; those hired first grumble. 'The last will be first, and the first last.'

title: Jesus foretells his death a third time
summary: Going up to Jerusalem, Jesus says he will be condemned, handed to the Gentiles to be mocked, flogged and crucified, and raised on the third day.

title: The mother of James and John makes a request
summary: She asks for her sons to sit at Jesus' right and left; Jesus teaches that the great must be servants, as the Son of Man came to serve and give his life as a ransom for many.

title: Jesus heals two blind men near Jericho
summary: Two blind men by the roadside cry 'Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!' and Jesus, moved with pity, touches their eyes.

title: The triumphal entry
summary: Jesus rides into Jerusalem on a donkey and a colt from Bethphage; crowds spread cloaks and branches and shout 'Hosanna to the Son of David!'

title: Jesus cleanses the temple
summary: Jesus drives out the money-changers ('a den of robbers'), heals the blind and lame, and defends the children's Hosannas.

title: Jesus curses the fig tree
summary: Finding only leaves, Jesus says 'May no fruit ever come from you again!' and it withers at once; with faith you could tell a mountain to be cast into the sea.

title: The authority of Jesus challenged
summary: The chief priests and elders ask by what authority he acts; Jesus asks them whether John's baptism was from heaven or from man, and they will not answer.

title: The parable of the two sons
summary: One son refuses to work in the vineyard but goes; the other says 'I go, sir' but does not. Tax collectors and prostitutes go into the kingdom before you.

title: The parable of the wicked tenants
summary: Tenants beat the owner's servants and kill his son; 'the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.' The chief priests realize he is speaking about them.

title: The parable of the wedding feast
summary: Invited guests refuse a king's wedding feast for his son, so he invites all from the roads; a man without a wedding garment is cast out. 'Many are called, but few are chosen.'

title: Paying taxes to Caesar
summary: Pharisees and Herodians try to trap him; looking at a denarius, Jesus says 'Render to Caesar the things that are Caesar's, and to God the things that are God's.'

title: Sadducees ask about the resurrection
summary: Asked whose wife a woman married to seven brothers will be, Jesus says in the resurrection they neither marry nor are given in marriage; God is the God of the living.

title: The great commandment
summary: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, soul and mind; and love your neighbor as yourself. On these two hang all the Law and the Prophets.

title: Whose son is the Christ?
summary: If David calls the Christ 'Lord' (Psalm 110), how is he his son? No one can answer, and no one dares ask him more questions.

title: Hypocrisy of the scribes and Pharisees
summary: Do what they teach but not what they do; they love places of honor. Call no one teacher or father; whoever exalts himself will be humbled.

title: The seven woes
summary: Woes to the scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites: they tithe mint but neglect justice, strain out a gnat and swallow a camel, and are like whitewashed tombs.

title: Lament over Jerusalem
summary: 'O Jerusalem, Jerusalem... How often would I have gathered your children together as a hen gathers her brood under her wings.'

title: Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple
summary: Not one stone of the temple buildings will be left upon another.

title: Signs of the end of the age (Olivet Discourse begins)
summary: On the Mount of Olives: wars, famines and earthquakes are the beginning of birth pains; the gospel will be proclaimed to all nations, and then the end will come.

title: The abomination of desolation
summary: When you see the abomination spoken of by Daniel, flee to the mountains; there will be great tribulation and false christs. 'Wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather.'

title: The coming of the Son of Man
summary: The sun will be darkened and stars fall; the Son of Man will come on the clouds with power and glory, and angels will gather the elect with a loud trumpet call.

title: The lesson of the fig tree
summary: When the fig tree's branch puts out leaves, summer is near; heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not.

title: No one knows that day and hour
summary: As in the days of Noah; one will be taken and one left. Stay awake, for the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect, like a thief.

title: The faithful and wise servant
summary: Blessed is the servant his master finds at work; the wicked servant who says 'My master is delayed' will be cut in pieces, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.

title: The parable of the ten virgins
summary: Five wise virgins bring oil and five foolish do not; when the bridegroom comes at midnight, the foolish are shut out. Watch, for you know neither the day nor the hour.

title: The parable of the talents
summary: Servants given five, two and one talent; the first two double theirs ('Well done, good and faithful servant'), the third buries his and is cast out.

title: The final judgment (the sheep and the goats)
summary: The Son of Man separates the nations as a shepherd separates sheep from goats: 'As you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me.'

title: The plot to kill Jesus
summary: Two days before Passover the chief priests and elders gather at the palace of Caiaphas to arrest Jesus by stealth, 'but not during the feast.'

title: Jesus anointed at Bethany
summary: At the house of Simon the leper a woman pours expensive ointment on his head; the disciples call it waste, but Jesus says she has prepared him for burial.

title: Judas agrees to betray Jesus
summary: Judas Iscariot goes to the chief priests, who pay him thirty pieces of silver.

title: The Passover with the disciples (the betrayer foretold)
summary: The disciples prepare the Passover; at the meal Jesus says one of them will betray him. Judas asks 'Is it I, Rabbi?' and Jesus replies 'You have said so.'

title: Institution of the Lord's Supper
summary: Jesus breaks bread ('this is my body') and gives the cup ('my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins').

title: Jesus foretells Peter's denial
summary: After singing a hymn they go to the Mount of Olives; Jesus says all will fall away and Peter will deny him three times before the rooster crows.

title: Jesus prays in Gethsemane
summary: Jesus prays three times, 'let this cup pass from me; nevertheless, not as I will', while Peter, James and John fall asleep.

title: The betrayal and arrest of Jesus
summary: Judas betrays Jesus with a kiss; a disciple cuts off the high priest's servant's ear ('all who take the sword will perish by the sword'), and all the disciples flee.

title: Jesus before Caiaphas and the council
summary: False witnesses testify; under oath Jesus says they will see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of Power. The high priest tears his robes; they spit on and strike him.

title: Peter denies Jesus
summary: In the courtyard Peter denies Jesus three times, the last with an oath; the rooster crows and he goes out and weeps bitterly.

title: Jesus delivered to Pilate
summary: In the morning the chief priests and elders bind Jesus and hand him over to Pilate the governor.

title: Judas hangs himself
summary: Judas regrets it, returns the thirty pieces of silver and hangs himself; the priests buy the potter's field (the Field of Blood) with the money.

title: Jesus before Pilate
summary: Pilate asks 'Are you the King of the Jews?' ('You have said so'); Jesus gives no answer to the accusations, and the governor marvels.

title: The crowd chooses Barabbas
summary: Pilate offers to release Jesus or Barabbas; his wife warns him about a dream; the crowd cries 'Let him be crucified!' and Pilate washes his hands.

title: The soldiers mock Jesus
summary: The soldiers put a scarlet robe and crown of thorns on him and mock him: 'Hail, King of the Jews!'

title: The crucifixion
summary: Simon of Cyrene carries the cross to Golgotha; the soldiers divide his garments, the sign reads 'This is Jesus, the King of the Jews', and passers-by, priests and robbers mock him.

title: The death of Jesus
summary: Darkness from the sixth to the ninth hour; Jesus cries 'Eli, Eli, lema sabachthani?' and dies. The temple curtain tears, the earth shakes, tombs open, and the centurion says 'Truly this was the Son of God!'

title: The burial of Jesus
summary: Joseph of Arimathea, a rich disciple, asks Pilate for the body and lays it in his own new tomb, rolling a great stone to the door.

title: The guard at the tomb
summary: The chief priests and Pharisees fear the disciples will steal the body; Pilate gives them a guard, and they seal the stone.

title: The resurrection
summary: Mary Magdalene and the other Mary find an angel sitting on the rolled-back stone: 'He is not here, for he has risen.' The risen Jesus meets them on the way.

title: The report of the guard
summary: The chief priests bribe the soldiers to say the disciples stole the body while they slept, a story still told 'to this day'.

title: The Great Commission
summary: On a mountain in Galilee the risen Jesus tells the eleven: 'Go therefore and make disciples of all nations... I am with you always, to the end of the age.'
